_comment: Rulebook mechanics that Action NAMES reference but which are not glossary keywords (so they have no entry in keywords.json). Matched case-insensitively against an action's name/description so the app can explain them. Text is condensed from the verified digests in ../rules.

mechanics.name: Optical Camouflage
mechanics.text: A stealth state rather than a token. A unit enters it by performing an Action that activates Optical Camouflage, or by deploying straight into it. On activation, swap the unit for its Optical Camouflage model and remove every Hexagon Token from it. While camouflaged, any Melee, Firing or Explosion Damage attack aimed at it must Scan first: if the Scan fails the attack fails outright, and a failed attack skips every step against the defender while the attacker still pays its own costs such as Ammo, Charge and Detonation. A unit whose Electronic Value is 0 or a dash cannot target it at all, because it cannot start the Scan counter-roll. Attacks that hit every unit in range need no Scan. The camouflage model marks only a suspected position, so the real unit may be elsewhere.

mechanics.name: Revealed
mechanics.text: Leaving Optical Camouflage. Swap the camouflage model back for the unit model. Four things reveal a unit and then let it make Manifestation Movement: its own Reveal Common Action, performing any Action that lacks the Silence keyword (Maneuvering counts, including a facing change with no movement), an enemy ending a move in contact with its base, and a successful enemy Scan. Passive Actions and Interception do not reveal it. Destroying the Part that performed the activating Action reveals it in place with no Manifestation Movement.

mechanics.name: Manifestation Movement
mechanics.text: The move a unit makes the instant it is Revealed. Because the Optical Camouflage model only marked a suspected position, the unit may appear up to X grids away, where X is the Stealth Value of the Action that activated the camouflage, so Stealth 2 means up to 2 grids and Stealth 0 means it appears where it stood. It is Teleportation Movement, so terrain and units in between are ignored. If the new position still meets the incoming attack's Range and Line of Sight requirements the attack carries on from there; if it does not, the attack fails.

mechanics.name: Scanning
mechanics.text: Reveals enemy units in Optical Camouflage and strips Low Profile Tokens. Designate an enemy that is in Optical Camouflage or bearing a Low Profile Token, then make an Electronic Counter-roll as the Initiator. On success: camouflaged targets are Revealed (they then make Manifestation Movement), and Low Profile Tokens are removed. Only token-based Low Profile can be scanned away; aura-based Low Profile cannot. Every Mech has Scan as a Common Action, and attacking a camouflaged unit forces a Scan first.

mechanics.name: Electronic Counter-roll
mechanics.text: Both sides roll Yellow Dice equal to their Electronic Value (a Mech's is the sum of all its Parts). The Initiator wins with more Lightning; if Lightning ties, more Light Hit; if both tie, the Initiator still wins. The Initiator must win for the action's effect to apply. Electronic Value 0 cannot initiate; a dash ('-') cannot be targeted. Strength +X adds X dice to the Initiator. Focus (1 Link) can reroll these dice. Electronic Warfare actions ignore Terrain and Line of Sight completely, so only Range matters. In Offensive Stance hollow faces count as valid results on these rolls too.

mechanics.name: Reboot
mechanics.text: The only action a Shutdown mech may take. It restores 1 Link and lets you change stance, but leaves the mech with just 1 Action Tick of the chosen Timing.

mechanics.name: Parry
mechanics.text: A melee-only defence. The defender designates a Part with a Parry Value as the target Part and adds that many White dice to the Defense Roll. Not available while in Shutdown or against a Back Attack. If a Black Die still decides the Part, the Parry dice only apply when it matches.

mechanics.name: Focus
mechanics.text: Spend 1 Link to reroll dice on any roll, including the Black part-locator die. You may not voluntarily spend down to 0 Link (you need the cost plus one), but damage-driven loss can reach 0, which immediately forces Shutdown stance.

mechanics.name: Crush
mechanics.text: Only Large (3x3) units can Crush, and only units smaller than themselves. Moving into an occupied grid forces a Crush: the victim takes Forced Movement of 1 grid, or swaps places if it cannot move, or is destroyed outright if it cannot be moved at all. The mover then enters the grid and its Movement Action ends immediately. Crushing also destroys destructible terrain.

mechanics.name: Penetration
mechanics.text: The damage step every attack builds toward. After Damage Resolution, any Heavy Hit or Light Hit left unoffset causes Penetration on the target Unit or Part. With no Structure Value it is Destroyed at once. With a Structure Value it takes a Damaged Token, or is Destroyed instead if it already had one, so health runs Intact to Damaged to Destroyed and the amount of leftover damage never changes that step. While Damaged, a Part rolls its Structure Value rather than its Armor Value for White Dice in Defense. Hit and Penetration are separate: damage offset by Defense counts as a Hit with no Penetration, so On-Hit riders such as Concussion and Knockback still fire, while damage offset by Dodge counts as neither.

mechanics.name: Surplus Damage
mechanics.text: Once a Penetration has happened, every Heavy Hit and Light Hit still unoffset is Surplus Damage. On its own it does nothing: it matters only when the Action carries a Surplus Damage keyword such as Mutilation, Cleaving or Scatter-shot, which spend it per Section 4.8. Those keywords are why an attack can roll far past what it needed and turn the excess into a second determined Part rather than wasting it.

mechanics.name: Integrity Loss
mechanics.text: A Mech reduced to 2 or fewer remaining Parts suffers Integrity Loss. It still acts as normal for the rest of the Round in which that happened, then is removed during that Round's End Phase, before Token Management and scoring. Destroying the Torso is different and kills the unit outright. Every other Part destroyed flips its card face-down, stops counting toward any Value, and costs 1 Link, and a Mech whose Link reaches 0 drops straight into Shutdown Stance.

mechanics.name: Break Away
mechanics.text: The movement tax for leaving a Melee Lock. A unit is Melee Locked when an adjacent enemy with a Melee Action has Line of Sight to it, which means almost any Mech outside Shutdown Stance, since all Mechs have Punch/Kick. A locked unit cannot perform Firing Actions at all. When it makes Basic Movement it pays 1 extra Movement Range each time it exits a grid while locked, and 1 extra for every unit locking it at that moment, so leaving two lockers costs 2 extra. Flying Movement ignores Melee Lock completely and Forced Movement ignores the extra cost. Aerial units and units in Optical Camouflage cannot be Melee Locked.

mechanics.name: Ammo and Charge
mechanics.text: Two separate token economies printed as icons on an Action. Ammo caps how many times an Action can be used: place one face-up Ammo Token per Ammo Icon at deployment, flip one face-down per use, and once they are all spent the Action cannot be performed. Volley X spends one Ammo Token per Projectile launched. Some Actions replenish Ammo by naming a Unit or Part and flipping consumed tokens back face-up, never above the starting number. Charge is a one-shot state instead: the token starts face-down, the Charge Action flips one named Part's token face-up, only one Part per Charge Action, and it cannot be Charged again until spent. An Action with a Charge-conditional effect may consume it by flipping the token back down.

mechanics.name: Screeching
mechanics.text: An Electronic Attack that costs the target Link. Like all Electronic Warfare it ignores Terrain and Line of Sight and needs only Range, and it resolves as an Electronic Counter-roll with the attacker as Initiator. It is one of the four things that take Link away, alongside Focus, Part Destruction and Concussion, and it is one of the three that can drive Link all the way to 0, which immediately forces the target into Shutdown Stance. Focus can never do that, because a voluntary reroll cannot spend your last point.

mechanics.name: Remote Access
mechanics.text: The second way to take a Terminal, and a Universal Action every Mech has in the Terminals missions. Perform it in the End Phase with the Torso at Range 4 for 1 action point, then make an Electronic Counter-roll against the Terminal, whose Electronic Value is 3. Success counts as accessing it. The alternative is Direct Access: at the End Phase you hold a Terminal if one of your Mechs outside Shutdown Stance or one of your Drones is inside its Tactical Zone and no enemy unit is. Either way a Terminal can only be accessed once per Round, its token flips face-down when taken, and every Terminal token flips back face-up at the End Phase.

mechanics.name: Detonation
mechanics.text: A projectile resolving its payload. Detonation destroys the projectile itself. Explosion damage hits everything in the affected grid(s) with no line-of-sight or facing requirement and no protection dice; only the defender may Focus.

mechanics.name: Victory Points and winning
mechanics.text: Track Victory Points with VP tokens as they are earned. At the end of the game the side with more VP wins. If VP are equal, the winner is the side with more Mech Parts and Drones still on the board.

mechanics.name: Main Task Cards
mechanics.text: The Main Task sets the encounter objective and also prints both deployment zones. During setup draw 3 Main Task Cards, each side discards 1, and the remaining card is the mission. A card shows the Tactical Areas in play, both deployment zones (for example Black 3x5 and White 3x5 strips on opposite edges), the task text, the VP values, and which Task Item Tokens are used. All 10 from the core box are listed in the Missions tab.

mechanics.name: Secondary Task Cards
mechanics.text: Each player also picks 1 Secondary Task during setup, starting with the First Player, and scores it privately alongside the shared Main Task. The core box has 8 and all of them are in the Missions tab. Three ask you to designate one of your own mechs: Escort scores 3 VP if it survives, Weapons Test scores 1 VP each time it destroys a Part or a Drone, and Disposal Procedure scores 2 VP when it dies. Two target the enemy: Decapitation is worth 5 VP but your opponent picks which of their mechs is the target, while Bounty Hunt is worth 4 VP and you pick. Annihilation scores 2 VP per enemy mech and 1 VP per drone, Mercy scores 2 VP for destroying no enemy mech at all, and Potential Excavation Area scores 2 VP for holding a Tactical Zone you nominate. The card text is our English rendering of the printed Korean, so the physical card wins.

mechanics.name: Tactics Cards
mechanics.text: Six Tactics Cards come in the core box, each costing 30 points against your squad total: Additional Instructions and Battlefield Recovery (GOF), Hit and Run and Tactical Disposition (UN), System Repair and Remote Restart (RDL). To use one you add it to your squad during list building. The rulebook sets no limit on how many you may take, but it does limit how many you may play: each player may only use 1 Tactics Card per round. Taking more than the game has rounds is legal and simply wasted points. Each card carries a faction logo; the squad faction rule in 5.1 is written about Units and Pilots, and 5.4.2 says nothing about matching a Tactics Card to your faction, so whether you may play another faction's card is genuinely unclear. Agree it with your opponent.

mechanics.name: Ticks and the Action Opportunity
mechanics.text: Every time a Mech receives an Action Opportunity it generates 1 Maneuver Tick and 2 Action Ticks. A Maneuver costs the Maneuver Tick, a Short Action costs 1 Action Tick, a Medium costs 2, and a Long costs the Maneuver Tick plus both Action Ticks, which is why a Long Action rules out Maneuvering. Ticks are spent in order: once any Action Tick has gone the Maneuver Tick can no longer be used, so a Maneuver has to come first. The first Action of the Opportunity is the Starting Action and its Action Type must match the Timing on the dial; later Actions in the same Opportunity have no type restriction. Each Action on a Part may only be performed once per Opportunity. Extra Ticks are separate: they may only be used after every base Tick is spent, never combine with a base Tick to pay for one Action, only pay for their own Action Type when one is named, and may repeat an Action already performed.

mechanics.name: Automatic and Command Actions
mechanics.text: Every Action on a Drone card is marked with a boxed icon beside its name that says when it happens. An exclamation mark is an Automatic Action: it resolves by itself in the Automatic Phase without being told to. A question mark is a Command Action: it only happens if you spend a Command Token on that Drone in the Command Phase. An Action with neither box is Passive and is always on. Mechs generate 1 Command Token each and Drones receive them. A commanded Drone acts immediately and either moves or performs one Command Action, so an Automatic Action cannot be taken on a Command. A Drone that acted on a Command does not act again that round, which means spending a token on a Drone whose only weapon is Automatic trades that attack away for a move. Unspent Command Tokens are removed at the end of the phase.

mechanics.name: Activation order in the Action Phase
mechanics.text: Mechs act one at a time in Timing order, which never changes: Swift, Melee, Projectile, Firing, Movement, Tactical. Within one Timing the Pilot with the LOWEST Initiative Value at that Timing acts first, that number being the one printed under the Timing icon on the dial. If two Mechs share both the Timing and the Initiative Value, the First Player's Mech goes first and the sides then alternate until every Mech at that value has acted. A Mech with no Timing set never activates at all.

mechanics.name: Token duration colours
mechanics.text: The background colour printed on a Square or Hexagon Token says how long it lasts. Green stays in effect indefinitely until an Action or effect removes it. Yellow is flipped to its reverse side at the end of the round, and that reverse is usually red. Red is about to expire and is removed at the end of the round. So a yellow token lasts two rounds: it flips at the first End Phase and comes off at the second. Low Recognition is the green one, printed green on its face and red on its reverse. Fragile, Fire Control Jamming, Immobilized and Highlight Target are yellow, each printed yellow on its face and red on its reverse.

mechanics.name: Deployment
mechanics.text: Before the first round both players roll 2 dice and the side with more Hits becomes First Player and chooses which board edge to play from. The book gives no tie procedure, so a tie is normally re-rolled. The First Player then deploys a single Unit wholly within an unoccupied Grid of their own Deployment Zone, after which the players alternate one Unit at a time until one side has placed everything, at which point the other places all of its remaining Units. A Mech chooses its Stance as it is deployed and counts as Offensive if none is set, and a Unit able to activate Optical Camouflage may be deployed directly into it.

mechanics.name: Interception
mechanics.text: Interception is how Aerial Units such as Missiles and Projectiles are shot down. Intercept X on an Action puts X Interception Tokens on that Card at Deployment. Interception triggers the moment an enemy Aerial Unit Moves or is Launched, if either the starting Grid or the ending Grid of that movement is within the Action's Range. Each attempt spends one Token and attacks as a Firing Attack, except that the target must be the Unit that triggered it, no Forward Arc is required, line of sight always exists, and no Terrain or Unit Protection may be claimed. If the target survives, that unit MUST intercept again until its Tokens run out or the target is destroyed, and several units in range intercept in sequence. Tokens are never restored, so what is spent is gone for the rest of the game. A Passive Action with Intercept can only ever attack through Interception, never as a normal Firing Attack.

mechanics.name: The End Phase
mechanics.text: Four steps, in this order. First remove units: every Mech left with 2 or fewer Parts goes, along with anything that says it is removed at the end of the round, alternating from the First Player if the order could matter. Second, token management: remove all Red Square and Hexagon Tokens, flip all Yellow ones to their reverse side, and remove every Command Token. Third, check Tasks, award Victory Points and test the victory conditions including the round limit. Fourth, flip the First Player Token so the other side goes first, and begin the next round. A standard game runs five rounds, after which Victory Points are totalled.
